name: Oral Lp(a) Treatments
blurb: Muvalaplin and other pills that could replace injections.
title: Oral Lp(a) Treatments
answer: Muvalaplin is the first oral small molecule designed to lower Lp(a). Rather than stopping production, it blocks apolipoprotein(a) from attaching to the LDL-like particle. In phase 2 it lowered intact Lp(a) by up to about 86 percent, and its outcome trial, MOVE-Lp(a), is underway.

reading.body:
Muvalaplin is the first oral small molecule for lowering Lp(a), and it works by blocking assembly rather than production. In phase 2 it cut intact Lp(a) by up to about 86 percent. It is investigational and available only in clinical trials.

The mechanism explains the measurement problem. Lp(a) forms when apolipoprotein(a) binds to apolipoprotein B on an LDL-like particle, and muvalaplin interferes with that binding step, so less complete Lp(a) circulates. Because the drug acts on assembly rather than production, assays that detect intact particles show larger reductions than some standard tests. The same biology that makes the pill work makes its effect harder to read.

A daily pill would be simpler to take and to stop than an injection, with quick reversibility if side effects appear. The tradeoff is adherence, which a pill demands every day. None of this yet establishes that lowering Lp(a) prevents events. That question belongs to MOVE-Lp(a), the phase 3 outcome trial, which plans about 10,450 participants with an estimated readout around 2031.

The data covers one drug and one trial timeline. It does not report safety results, cost, or how muvalaplin compares with the RNA-based therapies and gene editing approaches listed alongside it.

explainer:
Lp(a) forms when apolipoprotein(a) binds to apolipoprotein B on an LDL-like particle. Muvalaplin interferes with that binding step, so less complete Lp(a) circulates. Because it acts on assembly rather than production, measuring its effect depends on the assay; tests that detect intact particles show larger reductions than some standard tests.

A daily pill has practical advantages, no injections and quick reversibility if side effects appear, and disadvantages, daily adherence. Like every Lp(a) drug, it must still show in its outcome trial that lowering Lp(a) prevents events.
